{"claims":[{"claim_text":"The doctrine designating corporations as artificial persons has given them a degree of power exceeding that of natural persons.","claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence":"The pernicious doctrine designating corporations as artificial persons has given them a degree of power exceeding that of natural persons."},
{"claim_text":"The document supports examining and pursuing ways to reduce the power of corporations.","claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence":"We should examine and pursue, in coalition with groups such as Programs on Corporations, Law and Democracy (POCLAD) and Alliance for Democracy, ways to reduce and eventually limit this power by defining persons only as living individuals."},
{"claim_text":"The document supports examining and pursuing ways to eventually limit the power of corporations.","claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence":"We should examine and pursue, in coalition with groups such as Programs on Corporations, Law and Democracy (POCLAD) and Alliance for Democracy, ways to reduce and eventually limit this power by defining persons only as living individuals."},
